_comment: The SECOND ascension site (plan-ascension-sites.md C1), and the proof that a site owns its price: this stone asks for level 25 and a finished 'Thin the Orc Line', where the village stone asks for level 30. Nothing in Go compares the two numbers any more — D1 retired P1, so the only entry rule left is what a stone authors, snapshotted onto the pick when the row is clicked and re-judged when the ten-second channel lands (sys/ascension_rows.go stash → sys/skills.go applyAscension). ⚑ AUTHORED KNOB-FOR-KNOB FROM ascension-stone.json, which is where the reasoning for every body/factors value lives; only the gates, the id, the name and the lines differ. ⚑ PLACEMENT IS MEASURED, NOT EYEBALLED (55.2, 20.2): 7.65 units from the FrontCaptain and 5.50 from the nearest other spawn, because `E` goes to the NEAREST interactable and C3 already paid for that lesson with two conversants 3 units apart; 2.54 units clear of the nearest prop; and 6.08 from the nearest hostile spawn, so a player reading the panel is not pulled out of it by a wandering elite (combat closes a conversation, D21). ⚑ ITS GATE IS ONLY AS LEGIBLE AS THE FALLBACK LINE BELOW until C2 lands, which is what C2 is for: a locked navigation row will then name the price itself instead of vanishing. ⚑ TEXT IS PLAIN AND [PLACEHOLDER], the TownCrier convention — §8 of the archived ascension plan still owes both stones a lore write, and D4's tone stands: a life laid down, never a sacrifice extracted. ⭐ THE `catalog` NODE CARRIES THE SAME GATE AS THE GREETING, and it is not redundant: present() makes the FIRST node whose conditions pass the greeting, and applyGrant validates a row against its NODE, so an ungated catalog node would both show the reward list to a level-1 character and let a crafted message stash a pick below the price. The unconditional preview stays LAST (L3).
